newsitem.title: USA: CSCE announces rule changes to milk futures.
newsitem.headline: CSCE announces rule changes to milk futures.

text.p: The New York Coffee, Sugar and Cocoa Exchange (CSCE) will change some of the rules of its BFP (Basic Formula Price) milk futures and options contracts, an exchange spokesman said.
The rule changes allow the addition of new trading months (January, March, May, July, September and November), removing the distinction between "regular" and "additional" delivery months.
A contract will now have a trading cycle of 13 months, with trading permitted in each calendar month.
The contract amendments, adopted by the CSCE Board of Managers and approved by the Commodities Futures Trading Commission (CFTC), become effective Monday, July 7, 1997 for the March 1998 contracts.

Additionally, rule amendments were approved changing the last trading day for the BFP milk options contract to the exchange's business day prior to the day on which the U.S. Agriculture Department (USDA) announces the BFP price.
Previously the last trading day for an option contract was the 15th calendar day of the contract month.

"The BFP milk futures contract is cash settled against the BFP and uniformity is generally sought in such cases between the last trading day of a futures contract and its corresponding options contract," exchange spokesman Terrence Gordon said.
The BFP is an index price calculated and announced monthly by the USDA and is the pricing mechanism for milk purchases and sales used by 90 percent of the U.S. dairy industry.
The BFP milk futures contract was launched by the CSCE on April 8, 1997 and BFP options began on April 11, 1997.
Open interest in the BFP milk futures contract rose to just over 1,000 contracts on June 25.
